messages:
Soren: quick follow-up from today's all-hands 0101
Soren: ok above glitch ignore. main points: people asked about concrete dates for API stability window, Console rollout, and Optimize beta metrics. collecting here to pin answers.
Nina: API stability window: no breaking changes between now and the Console beta launch. we have one minor deprecated field planned for late q3 but it's opt-in feature flag first.
Tom: to add: infra will open a short compatibility window when we flip default behavior for the field. migration doc + deprecation warning header will hit docs next week.
Jae: customers were specifically asking whether webhooks for audit logs change shape in the Console upgrade 1: we need to confirm parity.
Nina: webhook payload shape will remain backwards-compatible. new fields will be added under a top-level "meta" object so old parsers ignore them. we'll publish an example payload in the migration checklist.
Soren: great. Optimize question: are the beta metrics going to include per-route cost delta estimates? several PMs want a quick cost delta number before enabling suggestions.
Nina: yes 1: Optimize beta will surface an estimated per-100k-token cost delta for suggested quantization/routing combos. the estimate is a conservative median with a 95% confidence band.
Tom: note on accuracy: those estimates come from sampled microbenchmarks plus historical latency distributions. for Dedicated customers we can plug actual perf traces to refine estimates.
Jae: can customers opt out of sending perf traces? some will need to for compliance.
Nina: opt-out is supported. when opt-out is chosen, Optimize uses conservative defaults and wider confidence intervals. we'll label those estimates clearly.
Soren: rollout cadence: Console beta -> Optimize feature flag -> Optimize public beta. can we get expected weeks for each?
Nina: current plan: Console beta this month (2 weeks EA), feature flag gated rollout during week 3, public Optimize beta opens in week 6. GA targeted in Q4 pending regression signals.
Tom: capacity note: Dedicated pools may need manual scaling for EA tenants. we'll provide an "EA request" form and a recommended prewarming checklist.
Jae: can we include an example canary config? ops asked for a 1%/10%/100% ramp with auto-rollback on quality regression.
Nina: yes, checklist will include a 1% canary template, metrics to track (latency p99, token failure rate, quality regression score), and an example auto-rollback rule.
Soren: are we providing SDK helpers for the rollout flags or should teams implement toggles themselves?
Nina: SDK helper functions will land in the client libs before Console beta. we'll add a small code snippet in the migration guide:
Nina: ```python
# example usage
from redwood import RoutingClient
rc = RoutingClient()
rc.create_rollout(route_id, canary_percent=1, auto_rollback_conditions=[{"metric":"quality_score","delta_thresh":-0.02}])
```
Tom: deploy-bot: staging deploy for console-rollout branch succeeded.
deploy-bot: [notice] deployed console-rollout to staging at commit 8b7d1c2 1: smoke tests ok.
Soren: excellent. last ask: who owns the migration checklist review? calling out Nina + Jae + Tom. can each of you ack?
Nina: ack, i'll draft the checklist and post a PR.
Tom: ack, i'll add the prewarm + capacity notes.
Jae: ack, i'll collect customer-facing wording and compliance notes.
Soren: thank you  let's close after the PR review. I'll update the all-hands notes with these timelines later today.
